purpose: Frozen inventory of every bridge tool across both lanes. No tool may be removed until its replacement reaches migrated_verified. See docs/TOOL_MIGRATION.md.

tools.name: actor_delete
tools.description: Delete actors by name or name pattern (supports * and ? wildcards).

tools.name: actor_delete
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_delete_actor] Delete one actor by exact name. The legacy wildcard form has no native equivalent and is refused. Calling this tool is the confirmation the native tool requires.

tools.name: actor_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate an existing actor with an optional offset. Returns validation results by default.

tools.name: actor_modify
tools.description: Change an actor's location, rotation, scale, mesh, or visibility. Returns validation results by default.

tools.name: actor_modify
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_set_property] Change an actor's visibility through the native reflection writer. location, rotation, scale and mesh are not reachable from an actor label alone and are refused with the native call that does work.

tools.name: actor_organize
tools.description: Move actors into World Outliner folders.

tools.name: actor_selection
tools.description: Return the currently selected level actors and their world transforms.

tools.name: actor_snap_to_socket
tools.description: Snap one actor to another actor's named socket.

tools.name: actor_spawn
tools.description: Spawn an actor from an asset path at a given location/rotation/scale. Returns validation results by default.

tools.name: actor_spawn
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_spawn_actor] Spawn an actor from an asset path at a given location/rotation. asset_path becomes class_path. scale, name and folder have no native equivalent and are refused rather than dropped.

tools.name: ai_nav_rebuild
tools.description: Rebuild navigation data in the loaded level (RebuildNavigation console command).

tools.name: anim_batch_reanchor
tools.description: Dry-run a re-anchor across a folder or an explicit list of sequences and rank them by drift. This is the tool for the core workflow: edit the idle, then find which clips no longer line up with it. Each clip gets a verdict of aligned, drifted, or divergent. Divergent means the clip legitimately starts in a different pose rather than having drifted, so re-anchoring it would drag the character somewhere the animator never intended. A sequence that cannot be re-anchored is reported in skipped with a reason instead of aborting the sweep. Clips judged divergent are refused unless force is set.

tools.name: anim_blueprint_build_from_json
tools.description: Build an Animation Blueprint from a JSON specification. Creates the AnimBP asset with the given skeleton and populates the anim graph from the JSON spec (state machines, blend spaces, slots, etc.).

tools.name: anim_pose_delta
tools.description: Compare two AnimSequences bone by bone at a given frame and report the angular difference in degrees, sorted worst first. Use it to find which clips drifted after an idle was edited, and which bones are responsible. Read-only.

tools.name: anim_pose_snapshot
tools.description: Capture the local (parent-relative) pose of an AnimSequence at one frame: per-bone rotation quaternion, Rotator, translation, and scale. Use this to record an idle's anchor pose before editing it, so later drift can be measured against a known baseline. Read-only.

tools.name: anim_reanchor
tools.description: Report what re-anchoring a sequence to a reference pose would change: per-bone angular delta, how many keys each weight profile would touch, and which tracks would need key expansion first. Use it to preview a fix after editing an idle. Defaults to dry_run; set dry_run=false to write, which is refused when the clip is judged divergent. Additive sequences are refused outright. Defaults to the spine_01 subtree with root and pelvis excluded, because rebasing those breaks root motion and foot planting.

tools.name: anim_root_motion_analyze
tools.description: Measure root track drift on an AnimSequence: per-axis range, per-frame step distribution (mean/max/p95), a roughness ratio that separates smooth authored sway from per-frame step noise, a root-vs-pelvis comparison that flags motion baked onto root at export, a rotation_roughness that detects wobble independently of amplitude, and the bone compression codec. A missing root track is reported as a flag rather than an error, so clips whose root was stripped are still analyzed. Pass folder_path instead of sequence_path to sweep a folder, sorted by roughness descending. Reads import-time data, so runtime causes such as foot IK or decompression artifacts cannot appear here. Read-only.

tools.name: asset_info
tools.description: Return detailed info for a single asset: type, bounds, material slots, LOD count.

tools.name: asset_list
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_find_assets] List assets with optional filters. asset_type becomes type and name_pattern becomes name; path and recursive pass through unchanged.

tools.name: asset_list
tools.description: List assets with optional filters. Returns asset paths, types, and names.

tools.name: asset_load_diagnostics
tools.description: Diagnose asset loads, Blueprint generated classes, dependencies, referencers, and script class availability.

tools.name: asset_save_many
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_save] Save the explicit asset paths passed in, through the native save command.

tools.name: asset_save_many
tools.description: Save only the explicit asset paths passed in. Safer than project-wide save-all.

tools.name: audio_component_add
tools.description: Add an AudioComponent to a Blueprint, optionally assigning a SoundBase asset and auto-activate. Compiles and saves.

tools.name: batch_operations
tools.description: Execute multiple tool calls in a single request with shared validation.

tools.name: batch_spawn
tools.description: Spawn multiple actors in one call. Each spawn definition uses the same format as actor_spawn.

tools.name: behavior_tree_create
tools.description: Create a BehaviorTree asset bound to an existing Blackboard, optionally building its node graph from a BehaviorTreeBuilder JSON spec (26 node types: Selector/Sequence/SimpleParallel composites, MoveTo/Wait/etc tasks, Blackboard/Cooldown/etc decorators, services). Optionally adds keys to the blackboard first.

tools.name: blackboard_create
tools.description: Create a BlackboardData asset with typed keys (Bool, Int, Float, String, Name, Vector, Rotator, Object, Class).

tools.name: blueprint_add_event_dispatcher
tools.description: Create an event dispatcher (multicast delegate) with an optional parameter signature, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_add_function
tools.description: Create a user function graph on a Blueprint with typed inputs/outputs, then compile and save. Returns the function graph name.

tools.name: blueprint_add_interface
tools.description: Implement a Blueprint Interface on a Blueprint, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_add_variable
tools.description: Add a member variable to a Blueprint, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_build_from_description
tools.description: Build a Blueprint event graph from high-level pattern templates. Each step references a named pattern with optional parameters. Exec flow is auto-wired between steps. Available patterns: on_begin_play, print_string, print_float, get_actor_location, loop_print, move_actor_up

tools.name: blueprint_build_from_json
tools.description: Builds a Blueprint event graph from a JSON node/connection description. Supported node types: BeginPlay, PrintString, Delay, CallFunction. Node objects accept an optional 'params' key to set pin default values by PinName. Connections use 'nodeId.exec' format for exec pin wiring.

tools.name: blueprint_compile
tools.description: Compile a Blueprint and return success/failure with error details. Success means the compile ran, check 'compiled' and 'had_errors' for actual result.

tools.name: blueprint_component_remove
tools.description: Remove a component (SCS node) from a Blueprint; children re-parent to the removed node's parent. Compiles and saves.

tools.name: blueprint_component_rename
tools.description: Rename a component (SCS node) on a Blueprint, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_create
tools.description: Create a new Blueprint class with optional components and variables.

tools.name: blueprint_document
tools.description: Generate a human-readable text summary of a Blueprint's structure, variables, and components.

tools.name: blueprint_info
tools.description: Get detailed Blueprint structure: components, variables, functions, event graphs, parent chain.

tools.name: blueprint_inspect
tools.description: Read Blueprint structure: graphs, functions, variables, macros, interfaces, event dispatchers, components (SCS), nodes in a graph with pins and links, single node detail, or node search. Use before editing to resolve graph names, node GUIDs, and pin names.

tools.name: blueprint_list
tools.description: List Blueprint assets with optional filtering by path, name, and parent class.

tools.name: blueprint_node_add
tools.description: Add a node to a Blueprint graph. Returns the new node's GUID for pin wiring. node_type is a registered factory: CallFunction, Event, CustomEvent, VariableGet, VariableSet, Branch, Sequence, Knot, Comment, Cast, CreateWidget, SpawnActor, MacroInstance, MakeStruct, BreakStruct, Select, FormatText, SwitchEnum, SwitchInt, SwitchName, SwitchString, MultiGate, DoOnceMultiInput, InputAction, InputAxisEvent, InputKey, AddDelegate, RemoveDelegate, CallDelegate, and more. config keys are camelCase and depend on node_type: CallFunction {targetClass, functionName}; Event {parentClass, eventName}; CustomEvent {eventName, parameters?}; VariableGet/VariableSet {varName, scope?}; Cast {targetClass, purity?}; SpawnActor {actorClass}; CreateWidget {widgetClass}; MakeStruct/BreakStruct {structType}; Comment {text}; MacroInstance {macroBP, macroName}. EXCEPTION: input nodes use snake_case keys - InputAction {action_name, consume_input?}, InputAxisEvent {axis_name}, InputKey {key}. Class paths use /Script/Module.Class form. Compiles and saves.

tools.name: blueprint_node_delete
tools.description: Delete a node by GUID (links broken first), then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_node_move
tools.description: Move a node to a new graph position, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_node_set_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a node by GUID, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_pins_break
tools.description: Break all links on a single pin of a node, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_pins_connect
tools.description: Connect two pins between nodes. The connection is validated by UEdGraphSchema_K2::CanCreateConnection before linking - incompatible types fail cleanly with no graph change. Compiles and saves on success.

tools.name: blueprint_remove_event_dispatcher
tools.description: Remove an event dispatcher by name, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_remove_function
tools.description: Remove a user function graph by name, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_remove_interface
tools.description: Remove an interface implementation (deletes its generated function graphs), then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_remove_variable
tools.description: Remove a member variable from a Blueprint, then compile and save.

tools.name: blueprint_set_variable_default
tools.description: Set a member variable's default value, then compile and save.

tools.name: bridge_clear_log
tools.description: Reset the MCP output-log cursor marker. Does not delete or truncate the UE log.

tools.name: bridge_command_manifest
tools.description: Return command names currently registered in the live Unreal listener.

tools.name: camera_rig_create
tools.description: Add a camera rig to a Pawn/Character Blueprint using a preset: first_person (eye-height camera, pawn control rotation), third_person (300 spring arm with lag), top_down (800 arm at -60 pitch), or side_scroller (500 arm at -90 yaw). Compiles and saves.

tools.name: camera_shake_blueprint
tools.description:
Create a CameraShake Blueprint asset with oscillation parameters.
Shake presets: explosion, hit, earthquake, gunfire, footstep, ambient, electric_shock, glitch_shake.
Or set individual rot_pitch/yaw/roll_amp/freq, loc_x/y/z_amp/freq, fov_amp/freq values.

tools.name: camera_shake_play
tools.description: Play a camera shake during PIE. Requires PIE to be running.

tools.name: camera_shake_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a CameraShakeSourceActor in the level. Emits shake within inner/outer radius during PIE.

tools.name: camera_shake_trigger
tools.description: Spawn a C++ ShakeTriggerActor: plays camera shake when the player overlaps its trigger box during PIE. Python builds, C++ executes -- the reliable pattern.

tools.name: checkpoint_create
tools.description: Create a named save point (level save + metadata snapshot).

tools.name: checkpoint_restore
tools.description: Restore to a named checkpoint by undoing operations since it was created.

tools.name: clear_output_log
tools.description: Alias for bridge_clear_log.

tools.name: cloth_apply_fabric_profile
tools.description: Apply a bounded UE4.27 NvCloth fabric profile to exactly one embedded clothing asset, with a JSON backup, transaction, and package save. This command does not change cloth paint masks or the Physics Asset.

tools.name: cloth_apply_lower_leg_gradient
tools.description: Author a smooth UE4.27 Max Distance gradient from the trouser hem to the knee on one clothing asset. This intentionally activates formerly fixed lower-leg vertices, writes a full backup, and preserves the fabric profile and Physics Asset.

tools.name: cloth_inspect_asset
tools.description: Inspect a UE4.27 skeletal mesh and return render-section cloth bindings, physical cloth LOD counts, authoring masks, applied weight maps, NvCloth config, topology hash, and Physics Asset coverage.

tools.name: cloth_smooth_max_distance
tools.description: Apply topology-aware, non-expanding smoothing to one embedded clothing asset's UE4.27 Max Distance mask, preserving fixed anchors and writing a full backup before saving.

tools.name: console_effect
tools.description:
Toggle rendering features via console commands.
Commands: freeze_rendering, show_fps, screen_percentage, temporal_aa, fxaa, motion_blur, bloom, eye_adaptation, tonemapper, ssr, ao, dof, aa_quality, shadow_quality, view_distance_quality, post_process_quality.

tools.name: cpp_build
tools.description: Compile the project with UnrealBuildTool as a background job. Returns a job_id immediately; poll job_status for progress and structured compiler errors (file, line, code, message).

tools.name: cpp_class_create
tools.description: Generate a UCLASS header/source pair in a game module (UE4.27 wizard-style boilerplate with GENERATED_BODY and constructor). Does not compile; run cpp_build afterwards. New classes require an editor restart to load.

tools.name: data_table_create
tools.description: Create a DataTable for a row struct, optionally filling rows from DataTable JSON ([{"Name": "Row1", ...fields}]). Saves the table.

tools.name: data_table_fill_from_json
tools.description: Replace an existing DataTable's rows from DataTable JSON, then save. Returns the resulting row names.

tools.name: engine_source_read
tools.description: Read a line range from a UE4.27 engine source file on disk (path as returned by engine_source_search, relative to <EngineRoot>/Engine). Use to see full declarations, parameter lists, and comments. Works with the editor closed.

tools.name: engine_source_search
tools.description: Search the local UE4.27 engine C++ source on disk for a symbol declaration or regex. Covers plain C++ the reflection database misses (Slate widgets, FRunnable, editor utilities, macros). Returns file, line, matched text, and the #include path when derivable. Works with the editor closed.

tools.name: folder_hidden_list
tools.description: List Content Browser folders currently hidden by folder_hide.

tools.name: folder_hide
tools.description: Hide one or more /Game subfolders in the Content Browser (display-only: assets stay on disk, referenced, and cookable). Persists across editor restarts via Config/FolderVisibility.ini. Refuses to hide /Game itself.

tools.name: folder_show
tools.description: Unhide Content Browser folders hidden by folder_hide. Call with no arguments to unhide EVERYTHING (escape hatch).

tools.name: game_template_create
tools.description: Generate a playable game skeleton: gameplay framework (GameMode/Character/PlayerController/HUD with class defaults wired), a camera rig matching the template, an input preset, and optionally a new map and project default game mode. Templates: first_person, third_person, top_down, side_scroller. Returns a manifest of everything created.

tools.name: gameplay_framework_create
tools.description: Create a linked set of gameplay framework Blueprints (GameMode, Pawn or Character, PlayerController, GameInstance, HUD, GameState, PlayerState) named BP_<base_name><suffix>, with the GameMode's class defaults wired to the created pieces. Compiles and saves everything.

tools.name: gameplay_pattern_search
tools.description: Find reusable gameplay patterns in indexed Blueprints, widgets, and level actors using deterministic heuristics. Patterns include overlap logic, key-door flows, prompt widgets, objective chains, and interactables.

tools.name: gameplay_pie_start
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_pie_start] Request Play In Editor start. level_path is refused: the native command starts PIE in the current level and cannot load one first.

tools.name: gameplay_pie_start
tools.description: Launch a Play In Editor (PIE) session and wait until the game world is ready (up to 30s). Returns success once the PIE-ready log marker is found. Call this before gameplay_run_acceptance_tests or gameplay_telemetry_snapshot.

tools.name: gameplay_pie_status
tools.description: Report whether a PIE session is live, and if so the possessed pawn class, visible widgets, AI controller count and FPS. Poll this after gameplay_pie_start: that call returns as soon as the request is queued, because PIE cannot initialise while a handler holds the game thread.

tools.name: gameplay_pie_stop
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_pie_stop] Request Play In Editor stop.

tools.name: gameplay_pie_stop
tools.description: End the current PIE session.

tools.name: gameplay_run_acceptance_tests
tools.description: Run structured acceptance test predicates against a live PIE session. PIE must already be running (call gameplay_pie_start first). Returns pass/fail per predicate with observed value. Predicates: 'pawn_possessed:ClassName', 'widget_visible:WidgetName', 'log_contains:String', 'ai_state:ActorName:StateName', 'survive:N' (N seconds without crash).

tools.name: gameplay_telemetry_snapshot
tools.description: Capture the current PIE runtime state: new log lines since last snapshot, possessed pawn class, visible widget class names, AI controller states, and PIE world name. PIE must be running.

tools.name: help
tools.description: Show documentation for available tools.

tools.name: history_list
tools.description: Show operation history with timestamps and parameters.

tools.name: input_mapping_add
tools.description: Add an action or axis mapping to project input settings (saved to Config/DefaultInput.ini). Key names use FKey string form: W, SpaceBar, LeftMouseButton, MouseX, Gamepad_LeftTrigger, ...

tools.name: input_mapping_info
tools.description: Inspect Unreal input action and axis mappings. Use this to validate bindings like PF_Pause to Escape when physical key injection is unavailable.

tools.name: input_mapping_remove
tools.description: Remove action or axis mappings. Omit 'key' to remove every key bound to the name.

tools.name: input_preset_apply
tools.description: Apply a standard control scheme preset: first_person, third_person, top_down, or tank (WASD movement, mouse look where applicable, Jump/Fire/Interact actions). Idempotent.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a running background job (terminates its subprocess).

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List all background jobs started in this editor session, newest first.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Get a background job's status (running/succeeded/failed/cancelled), structured result (e.g. parsed compiler errors for cpp_build), and output tail.

tools.name: level_actors
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_find_actors] List actors in the current level. class_filter becomes type, name_filter becomes name, limit passes through. Native filters are substring matches, so wildcard patterns and folder filtering are refused.

tools.name: level_actors
tools.description: List actors in the current level with optional filters. Returns name, class, folder, and optionally transforms and components.

tools.name: level_new
tools.description: Create and load a new level (optionally from a template map), then save it. WARNING: switches the editor's loaded level; refuses if unsaved changes exist.

tools.name: level_outliner
tools.description: Return the World Outliner folder tree structure with actor counts per folder.

tools.name: level_save
tools.description: [COMPAT ALIAS -> puerts_save] Save the current level through the native save command. save_all has no native equivalent: puerts_save takes an explicit asset list instead.

tools.name: level_save
tools.description: Save the current level and optionally all dirty assets.

tools.name: material_apply
tools.description: Apply a material to an actor's mesh component. Returns validation by default.

tools.name: material_create
tools.description: Create a new material, a simple opaque surface, or a material instance. Provide parent and type 'instance' for instances.

tools.name: material_info
tools.description: Get detailed information about a material: parameters, textures, parent chain.

tools.name: material_instance_create
tools.description: Create a MaterialInstanceConstant from a parent material with optional scalar/vector/texture parameter overrides. Saves the instance.

tools.name: material_instance_set_params
tools.description: Set scalar/vector/texture parameters on an existing material instance, then save.

tools.name: material_list
tools.description: List materials in the project with optional filtering by path, name, and type.

tools.name: optimization_apply_low_risk_fixes
tools.description: Apply explicit candidates from optimization_fix_candidates. Dry run by default: it reports what it would do and changes nothing until dry_run is false. Setting save_assets writes the modified assets to disk, which a plain editor undo will not recover.

tools.name: optimization_asset_audit
tools.description: Scan project assets for common optimization risks: oversized textures, excessive material slots, missing LODs. Static analysis, so it needs no PIE session and no capture.

tools.name: optimization_asset_cost_rank
tools.description: Rank the meshes in the active level by likely scene cost, combining triangle counts, material slots and instance counts. Use to decide what to optimise first.

tools.name: optimization_before_after_verify
tools.description: Compare a baseline measurement against an after measurement for a candidate group, so an optimization can be shown to have worked rather than assumed to have. Modifies assets only when apply_candidates is true.

tools.name: optimization_camera_path_profile
tools.description: Move the viewport through named viewpoints, measure each, and rank them by cost. Use to find which part of a level is expensive rather than which subsystem.

tools.name: optimization_cpu_capture
tools.description: Run CPU-side overlays covering the game thread, animation, physics, Blueprint and particles, and return parsed findings. Use when quick triage shows Game rather than Draw or GPU as the dominant cost.

tools.name: optimization_fix_candidates
tools.description: Return low-risk fix candidates, kept separate from manual recommendations so an automated pass never touches anything needing judgement. Read-only: it proposes, it does not apply. Feed the result to optimization_apply_low_risk_fixes.

tools.name: optimization_generate_report
tools.description: Write a Markdown optimization report under Saved/. Give it a payload from an earlier capture, or omit the payload to run a fresh quick triage and report on that.

tools.name: optimization_gpu_capture
tools.description: Run GPU-focused console commands and capture the render viewmodes that explain GPU cost (shader complexity, overdraw, lighting). Use when quick triage shows GPU as the dominant frame cost.

tools.name: optimization_insights_trace_start
tools.description: Start an Unreal Insights trace. Pair with optimization_insights_trace_stop. Use for a timeline of CPU work across frames, which the stat overlays cannot show.

tools.name: optimization_insights_trace_stop
tools.description: Stop the active Unreal Insights trace and summarise the newest trace file when parser support is available. Returns the trace path either way.

tools.name: optimization_insights_trace_summary
tools.description: Summarise an Unreal Insights trace file already on disk. Give a path, or omit it to summarise the newest trace.

tools.name: optimization_memory_streaming_capture
tools.description: Run memory and texture-streaming overlays and return structured memory findings, optionally with an asset audit in the same pass. Use for hitching, streaming pops, or memory ceilings rather than frame cost.

tools.name: optimization_profilegpu_capture
tools.description: Run ProfileGPU and parse the per-pass GPU timing breakdown from its text or log output. This is the finest grained GPU measurement UE4.27 exposes without an external tool.

tools.name: optimization_quick_triage
tools.description: First-pass performance investigation: runs the triage console commands, captures overlays, optionally audits assets and the scene, then classifies findings against a frame budget. Run this before any targeted capture so the follow-up is aimed at the thread that is actually slow.

tools.name: optimization_rendering_capture
tools.description: Run render-thread and scene-rendering overlays (draw calls, visible primitives, init views) and return parsed findings. Use when the Draw thread rather than the GPU is the bottleneck.

tools.name: optimization_run_console_checklist
tools.description: Run a list of safe profiling console commands in order and return the parsed findings. Defaults to the standard triage set when no commands are given. Use this when you know which stat commands you want rather than running a full capture.

tools.name: optimization_scene_audit
tools.description: Inspect the open level for lighting, culling, tick and setup risks: dynamic lights, actors ticking every frame, missing culling distances. Complements the asset audit, which cannot see level composition.

tools.name: optimization_stat_capture
tools.description: Capture stat and CSV profiler files over a duration, where UE4.27 exposes them. Use when you need a recording across time rather than a single-frame reading.

tools.name: optimization_texture_harm_rank
tools.description: Rank textures by likely harm, following dependency trails from the active level so the ranking reflects what is actually loaded rather than everything on disk.

tools.name: optimization_tool_catalog
tools.description: Search the UE4.27 profiling command catalog. Each entry names a console command, the question it answers, when to reach for it, what a bad reading looks like, and what to do next. Start here when you do not yet know which capture to run. Filter by category or free-text query.

tools.name: optimization_viewmode_capture_set
tools.description: Capture an explicit set of optimization viewmodes as screenshots and restore the viewport afterwards. Use when you want specific views rather than the curated GPU set.

tools.name: optimization_visual_logger_ingest
tools.description: Parse Visual Logger output or log text for gameplay-heavy CPU clues. Use when the game thread is slow but the stat overlays do not say which gameplay system is responsible.

tools.name: optimization_vr_audit
tools.description: Audit against a VR refresh-rate budget, where the frame budget is far tighter than desktop and forward rendering constraints apply. Use for any VR target rather than the desktop audits.

tools.name: pie_agent_expect
tools.description: Poll declarative actor_count, player counter, and log regex assertions in-engine until they pass or the deadline expires.

tools.name: pie_agent_look_at
tools.description: Point the PIE player camera at a location or named actor.

tools.name: pie_agent_move_to
tools.description: Walk the PIE player pawn to a location or named actor along a nav path, with a straight-line fallback. Resolves when arrived or timed out.

tools.name: pie_agent_observe
tools.description: Capture a PIE snapshot: pawn transform and velocity, nearby actors with physics and collision state, widgets, player counters, and Output Log tail.

tools.name: pie_agent_press
tools.description: Press an action mapping through live InputComponent bindings, or a raw key through the PlayerController, then release it after the requested hold.

tools.name: pie_agent_record_start
tools.description: Start frame-accurate spawn, destroy, and overlap event recording for filtered actor classes.

tools.name: pie_agent_record_stop
tools.description: Stop PIE event recording and return the timestamped event list.

tools.name: pie_agent_replay
tools.description: Replay a PIE agent script with a fixed random seed for regression testing, or export the current session script.

tools.name: pie_agent_status
tools.description: Poll the current PIE agent asynchronous operation. Operation id 0 means the latest operation.

tools.name: placement_validate
tools.description: Check actors for gaps, overlaps, and alignment issues.

tools.name: pp_preset
tools.description:
Apply a named post-processing preset. Creates or updates a PP volume.
Presets: horror, cyberpunk, noir, dream, underwater, surveillance, vhs_glitch, damage, drunk, frozen, nuclear, sepia, cinematic, neon, thermal.

tools.name: pp_volume_modify
tools.description: Modify an existing PostProcessVolume's settings. Settings merge with existing values.

tools.name: pp_volume_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a PostProcessVolume with full settings control. Supports bloom, exposure, color grading, DOF, chromatic aberration, grain, vignette, motion blur, SSR, lens flare, and more.

tools.name: project_enable_plugins
tools.description: Enable one or more plugins in the current .uproject and report whether an editor restart is required.

tools.name: project_index_query
tools.description: Search the cached project intelligence index. Use this before editing to find existing assets, Blueprint structures, dependencies, and patterns.

tools.name: project_index_rebuild
tools.description: Rebuild the lightweight project intelligence index under Saved/MCP/index. Scans assets, Blueprints, materials, widgets, level actors, and design memory using existing read-only bridge handlers.

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Return current UE project name, engine version, project path, content directory, and loaded level.

tools.name: project_semantic_diff
tools.description: Compare indexed before/after snapshots for semantic changes in Blueprints, widgets, materials, level actors, and dependencies. If snapshots are omitted, compares cached index data against a fresh read.

tools.name: project_settings_maps
tools.description: Set default maps and game mode: game default map, editor startup map, and/or global default game mode. Persists to Config/DefaultEngine.ini.

tools.name: prompt_generate
tools.description: Generate complete Unreal Engine 4.27 gameplay systems from a natural language prompt. Creates Blueprints, Widget Blueprints, materials, data assets, maps, actors, and input mappings. Supports genres: puzzle_fighter, menu_system, horror, platformer, inventory, generic. Use dry_run=true to preview the build spec without creating any assets.

tools.name: prompt_spec_list

tools.name: puerts_blueprint_build
tools.description: [PRIMARY NATIVE IPC] Create or update a compiled Blueprint actor asset from one JSON spec: parent class, components with their template properties, and an event graph. A component property takes the value in its own reflected shape, and an asset reference as an object path string, so a StaticMeshComponent can be given a mesh and materials. Member variables are declared the same way and are reachable from the graph through VariableGet and VariableSet nodes. Supported graph node types are BeginPlay, Tick, ActorBeginOverlap, ActorEndOverlap, PrintString, CallFunction, Operator, Delay, Branch, Sequence, Comment, Event, CustomEvent, VariableGet, VariableSet, Cast, Select, Knot, MakeStruct, BreakStruct, FormatText, SpawnActor, SwitchInt, SwitchString, MultiGate, DoOnceMultiInput and InputKey; anything else is rejected before the asset is touched. InputKey binds a literal FKey (params.fkey_name, for example "LeftShift") and needs no project input mapping, which is why it is the one input node type advertised. Rerunning the same spec converges: the asset is loaded rather than duplicated, an existing component or variable of the same name and type is left alone, and the event graph is rebuilt from the spec. A component or variable that exists under a different type is an error, never a silent retype. Every graph connection must resolve to real pins: the response's graph.connection_count is the number of links actually made, and any shortfall against the number requested fails the build with the dropped pairs named in errors and in graph.unresolved_connections, so a graph with a hole in it is never saved. A pure node has no exec pins, and a const BlueprintCallable UFUNCTION that returns a value is pure. Assets are limited to /Game/MCPGenerated/. Response reports compile status with compiler errors and warnings; the asset is only saved when it built clean.

tools.name: puerts_widget_build
tools.description: [PRIMARY NATIVE IPC] Create or replace a compiled UMG Widget Blueprint from one JSON widget tree. The tree is a hierarchy of typed, named widgets: each carries optional widget-intrinsic properties and an optional slot object holding the layout its parent owns. The whole tree is validated before any asset is touched, so an unsupported widget type, a duplicate name, a property the type does not have, or a child under a leaf widget is a rejection rather than a half-built asset. Rerunning a spec converges by replacing the tree of the asset already at that path; unlike a Blueprint's components and variables, a widget tree has no per-widget identity to merge against, so the spec is the whole tree. Assets are limited to /Game/MCPGenerated/. The response reports the hierarchy read back out of the built asset, not the request, along with generated_class_path, which is the class a graph needs to create the widget at runtime.
